title: Fixed sensor offsets kept vapor pressure contrast signs in North Wales domes in August and September 2021
abstract: We tested whether fixed sensor calibration offsets could remove a monthly reversal in the light-minus-dark vapor pressure contrast in a public ozone and warming experiment. We used 1,464 complete hours and a shared ambient reference for three heated domes. We allowed fixed temperature offsets up to 0.2 C and fixed relative humidity offsets up to one percentage point per sensor. Conservative bounds retained negative August and positive September contrasts under four light rules. All 12 September-minus-August bounds were above zero. At the primary light rule, lower bounds on this change were 0.103 to 0.145 kPa. Bounds with errors that can vary each hour included zero in all 36 tests. A grid derivative bound and a clipping bound enclosed unsampled offsets. Thus fixed calibration offsets within these assumed limits cannot explain the recorded signs, but changing errors remain possible. This is a sensitivity test of prior evidence, not independent replication or a plant mechanism test. One site-year, unreplicated chambers, shared weather, unknown calibration and possible gap filling limit inference. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate bounds, validation and a figure. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Conservative fixed-offset bounds retain the monthly signs; independent reading-error intervals include zero. The points are recorded contrasts, and the ranges are deterministic error bounds, not confidence intervals. Primary light rule: at least 20 micromoles per square metre per second.

citations.reason: Tests its recorded monthly reversal with a new fixed calibration offset model. The source observations overlap; no prior code is reused.
